question: Parent here: what's the biggest AOTC we could get for one kid, and is any of it refundable?
reference_answer: The American Opportunity Tax Credit is worth up to $2,500 per eligible student: 100% of the first $2,000 of qualified expenses plus 25% of the next $2,000. Up to 40% of it, $1,000, is refundable.

sources.title: IRS: Education credits questions and answers

question: Part of my scholarship covered my on-campus housing. Do I have to treat that part as income?
reference_answer: Yes. Scholarship money used for room and board is taxable income. Only amounts used for qualified expenses, such as tuition, required fees and required course materials, are tax-free for a degree candidate.

sources.title: IRS Topic no. 421, Scholarships, fellowship grants, and other grants

question: My income-driven plan will wipe out my remaining balance in 2027. Will that be tax-free federally like it was a few years ago?
must_not_include: still tax-free under the American Rescue Plan
not taxable under the American Rescue Plan
reference_answer: Probably not. The American Rescue Plan Act's exclusion covered loans forgiven on or before December 31, 2025. IDR forgiveness in 2026 or later is generally taxable as cancellation of debt income, and you may get a Form 1099-C.

sources.title: Taxpayer Advocate Service: What to Know about Student Loan Forgiveness and Your Taxes
sources.section: Student loan debt cancelled after December 31, 2025, may be taxable income

question: I work for a nonprofit and I'm close to Public Service Loan Forgiveness. Does the IRS count the forgiven balance as income?
reference_answer: No. Public Service Loan Forgiveness is not taxable: the Taxpayer Advocate Service lists it among forgiveness types that don't create a tax liability, unlike income-driven repayment forgiveness.

sources.title: Taxpayer Advocate Service: What to Know about Student Loan Forgiveness and Your Taxes
sources.section: Why this matters: not all loan forgiveness is taxable

question: Does the money I earned in my work-study job raise my Student Aid Index?
reference_answer: No. Federal Work-Study earnings are an income offset in the SAI formula, so they're subtracted from income. Schools report FWS earnings to the Department, which passes them to the FAFSA system.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 3: Student Aid Index (SAI) and Pell Grant Eligibility

question: I'm in a master's program. Which education credit can I use, and why not the AOTC?
must_not_include: grad students can claim the AOTC
reference_answer: The Lifetime Learning Credit is the usual option for graduate school. The AOTC is limited to students who haven't completed the first four years of postsecondary education and to four tax years per student, while the Lifetime Learning Credit has no limit on years and covers graduate courses.

sources.title: IRS: Education credits questions and answers

question: What's the max I can write off for student loan interest, and do I need to itemize?
reference_answer: You can deduct the smaller of $2,500 or the interest you actually paid. It's an adjustment to income, so you don't need to itemize, though it phases out at higher incomes.

sources.title: IRS Topic no. 456, Student loan interest deduction

question: What does the amount in Box 5 of the tuition statement from my college mean?
reference_answer: Box 5 of Form 1098-T shows the total scholarships and grants your school administered and processed for your cost of attendance. Payments are in Box 1, which isn't reduced by Box 5.

question: I'm 19 and my mom lists me as her dependent. Am I allowed to take the American Opportunity credit on my own taxes?
must_not_include: yes, you can claim it yourself
reference_answer: No. If someone else claims you as a dependent, you can't claim the AOTC. The person who claims you can claim it, and expenses you paid are treated as paid by them.

sources.title: IRS Publication 970 (2025), Tax Benefits for Education
sources.section: Chapter 2: Who can claim a dependent's expenses

sources.title: IRS: Education credits, AOTC and LLC

question: I'm independent and my income was too low to need to file a return. What happens to my Student Aid Index?
must_not_include: you can't file the FAFSA without a tax return
reference_answer: An independent student (and spouse) not required to file the tax return the FAFSA asks about is automatically eligible for a Maximum Pell Grant with an SAI of -1,500 for 2026-27, as long as other Pell requirements are met. Foreign non-filers are handled differently.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form

question: Our son owns his own 529 and he's a dependent. Do we list it as his asset or ours on the FAFSA?
reference_answer: List it as a parent investment. For a dependent student, a 529 designated for that student is reported with the parents' investments, not as the student's asset.

sources.title: 2026-27 FSA Handbook, Application and Verification Guide, Ch. 2: Filling Out the FAFSA Form

question: My 1098-T came in the mail. Does that mean I'm guaranteed to qualify for the AOTC?
reference_answer: No. A 1098-T just reports what your school received. Whether you can claim the AOTC depends on the rules: degree enrollment at least half-time, not having finished the first four years of college, no more than four tax years claimed, income limits, not being claimed as a dependent, and qualified expenses after subtracting tax-free aid. Form 8863 or a tax professional can confirm it.

sources.title: IRS: Education credits, AOTC and LLC
IRS Publication 970 (2025), Tax Benefits for Education
